transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I came in because I honestly can't see my studio, or really my life in general, getting back on track anymore. I just don't see it happening. It doesn't seem to matter how hard I work at it, or... or what kind of payment plan they put in front of me. I'm just out of options.
Have you been feeling like things will never get better or that there's no way out of your situation?

Yeah, exactly. That's pretty much what I meant. I just... I don't see a way out anymore. Like I said, no matter how much effort I put into the shop, or what the bank tries to offer me with these payment plans, it's a dead end. My life and my business are just... they're not going to get better.
How long have you been feeling this way about your situation?
Well, it's been going on since I took on the mortgage for the studio. That was a little over two years ago... I guess it's been about two years and two months now, to be exact.
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities, don't interest you anymore?

No, not really. I mean, I still like woodworking and being in the shop. It's just that the money problems make it hard to focus on the work itself, but I still enjoy doing it when I can actually get to it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two years?

Yeah, pretty much. Most days I wake up with this... this heavy, gray feeling already sitting on me. It's just there. And even when I'm in the shop, surrounded by the wood and the tools I used to love, it all just feels flat. I have to fight the urge to just stand there staring at the wall instead of working. It's been like that almost every day.

latest_inference.note: The patient has described a persistent depressed mood lasting most of the day, nearly every day, for over two years, with feelings of hopelessness and anhedonia (at least situational) related to their financial stress. This aligns with the criteria for recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe.
